solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Turned up with peripherals — rough stuff

indicators.note: turned here means flipped over, so the word beside it is read backwards

parts.note: the word up itself
computer peripherals include mice, the pointing devices plugged into a PC

explanation.surface: Something upended along with its edges turns out to be coarse material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' flips UP to PU; 'peripherals' is the computing sense, devices attached to a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a rough volcanic stone used for scrubbing skin, so it is literally rough stuff.

clue.text: Vote — and the symbol made? — with the thumb?

parts.note: a poll is a vote or ballot
the mark made on a ballot paper is an X, spelt out as the letter name ex

explanation.surface: A voter makes their mark on the ballot paper, perhaps pressing with the thumb.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross put on a ballot is X, written here as its letter name EX.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollex is the anatomical Latin term for the first digit of the hand, the human thumb.

clue.text: Basic intelligence that's evolved with more time

indicators.note: evolved means developed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Native intelligence that has developed as more time passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evolved' rearranges WITH, MORE and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother wit is innate common sense, the practical intelligence one is born with.

clue.text: Ugly woman engaged in vocation as artist

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a calling or call is a vocation
a hag is an ugly old woman

explanation.surface: An unattractive woman who has taken up art as her calling.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was a Russian-French painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Show some anger about 40% of trade in garden equipment

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: to simmer is to be quietly angry

indicators.note: forty per cent of a five-letter word is its opening two letters

explanation.surface: Someone getting cross about a share of the business in gardening tools.
explanation.walkthrough: '40% of' a five-letter word is its first two letters; 'about' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A strimmer is a powered line trimmer used for cutting grass edges, an item of garden kit.

clue.text: Comradeship that's remarkable at its prime

indicators.note: remarkable read as re-markable, able to be marked again in a new way, signals rearrangement

explanation.surface: Fellowship that is outstanding when it is at its peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' rearranges AT ITS PRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Team spirit is the sense of camaraderie and loyalty shared by members of a group.

clue.text: I especially note bedding — without question, integral

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is Latin for note well

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a quilt is bedding

explanation.surface: Someone making a point about bedding, unquestionably a fundamental part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes Q from QUILT, leaving UILT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built in is an integral part of the whole, not added on afterwards.

clue.text: Second eleven with energy and courage

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and a cricket or football side
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A reserve team playing with vigour and bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' looks like a reserve side, but the words split and each gives its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Moxie is American slang for nerve, pluck or determination, so it means courage.

clue.text: Ganymede's staff that's accommodating of Poseidon's realm mostly

definitions.note: read as Ganymede is, so the definition is the name Ganymede

indicators.note: accommodating means housing within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Poseidon ruled the sea, and saline describes salt water, the briny

explanation.surface: Ganymede the cupbearer's staff seems to hold part of the sea god's domain.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Ganymede's is 'is'; 'mostly' drops a last letter and 'accommodating' signals the container. Ganymede is not the mythical cupbearer but a Shakespearean alias.
explanation.definitionFit: In As You Like It, the heroine disguises herself as a youth and takes the alias Ganymede.

clue.text: Permit victor at Agincourt to describe his effect on the French?

definitions.text: to describe his effect on the French

parts.note: to let is to permit
Henry V, who won at Agincourt in 1415, appears as Prince Hal in Shakespeare's history plays

explanation.surface: Allowing the English king at Agincourt to sum up what he did to the French army.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry's archers killed huge numbers of French, so deadly is the adjective for his effect on them.

clue.text: Detests carrying wood containers

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to detest is to hate
box is a hardwood tree and its timber

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes having to haul wooden crates.
explanation.definitionFit: Hat boxes are cases for storing headwear, a kind of container.

clue.text: The pace faltered, having to accommodate unknown blockage to view ahead

indicators.note: to accommodate means to make room for inside, so a letter is placed within
faltered means stumbled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A runner slowed when an unexpected obstacle blocked the road ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faltered' gives EPATCHE before 'to accommodate' takes the unknown inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch over one eye blocks that eye's line of sight, so it obstructs forward vision.

clue.text: Staff organisation that prevents trade?

parts.note: a workplace where only union members may be hired; read literally, a store that is shut and so does no business

explanation.surface: A workforce arrangement that seems to stop commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a shop with its doors shut, literally preventing trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A union-only workplace arrangement restricts staffing to members, with the quip on a shut store.

clue.text: Long line encompassing a description of a gland

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to pine is to long or yearn

explanation.surface: A long line wrapped round a written account of a gland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encompassing' puts A inside PINE + L.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineal is the adjective naming the small cone-shaped gland in the brain that secretes melatonin.

clue.text: See 5
Intend nasty worn teapot, nothing less, to show ceramic design

parts.note: to will something is to intend it

indicators.note: nasty means badly made, so these letters are put in disorder
less means minus, so a letter is removed

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Planning to use a shabby old teapot to display a china pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges WORN TEAPOT and 'less' takes away one O.
explanation.definitionFit: Willow pattern is the classic blue-and-white Chinese-style decoration on porcelain plates.

clue.text: Segregate broken feature of DVD?

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Separating a damaged part of a disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges SEGREGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden bonus content tucked away on a DVD is known as an Easter egg.

clue.text: Our effort mostly taken on board by grumpy person

indicators.note: taken means received inside, so the pieces go within the ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the crossword shorthand for being on board
the word our itself

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a push is an effort

explanation.surface: Our attempt is largely accepted by a bad-tempered colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken on board' is the convention for going inside SS, a steamship; 'mostly' drops the last letter of the effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A sourpuss is an informal word for a sulky, sullen individual.

clue.text: Roaming brother is due to circle European islands

indicators.note: to circle means to go round, so one piece surrounds another
roaming means wandering about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wandering sibling is going to tour some European isles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roaming' gives OUTRHBRIDES, which 'to circle' wraps round the European letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Outer Hebrides are a chain of islands off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Iron extracted from monastery building for religious dwelling

indicators.note: extracted from means pulled out of, so letters are removed

parts.note: a refectory is the dining hall of a monastery
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Metal removed from a monastic building to make a home for clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking FE out of REFECTORY leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house provided for a rector, a parish priest.

clue.text: Garment with central part of cotton?

definitions.meaning: a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor times
the middle of cotton is TT, a doubled letter, which is a pair of identical letters

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing whose core is cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters of COTTON are TT, a pair of identical letters, i.e. a double letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet was a tight jacket; the word also names a matched pair, here two Ts.

clue.text: Goddess showing persistence of character?

parts.note: a letter that persists: the first letter of the alphabet, followed later by that same letter once more

explanation.surface: A deity displaying tenacity of temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter, not a personality: the letter, a time word meaning 'next', then the letter again.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the Greek deity of wisdom and war, patron of the city of Athens.

clue.text: Widow going again to collect first of children

indicators.note: to collect means to gather in, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: a fire relit is going again

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A widow remarrying to bring her eldest child back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' children is C, which goes inside RELIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Relict is an archaic word for a widow, the surviving spouse left behind.

clue.text: An amount of really crazy synthetic fabric

indicators.note: An amount of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A huge quantity of a stretchy man-made material.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is a brand of elastane, a stretchy man-made textile used in sportswear.

clue.text: Beer in France is carrying most weight

parts.note: stout is a dark beer
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A beer in France is the heaviest.
explanation.definitionFit: The stoutest person is the fattest, the one bearing the most bodily bulk.

clue.text: See 12
Relative penning hot comic strip

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: comic means farcical, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A family member drawing a racy cartoon strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' signals the anagram and 'penning' the container. 'strip' is a verb meaning undress, not a cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclothe someone is to undress them, a synonym of strip.

clue.text: Run off to cover one in chill — thermal jacket?

indicators.note: to cover means to stand in place of, so one piece replaces a letter

parts.note: ice is a chill
I is the Roman numeral for one
to flee is to run off

explanation.surface: Bolting to wrap someone up in the cold, wearing a warm top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' as in a stand-in: FLEE takes the place of the I in ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is a warm zip-up top made of synthetic pile, worn for insulation.

clue.text: Beautiful swimmer overturned my refusals in Aberdeen: 'Plenty hot to start with'

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: the word my itself
nae is Scots for no, so refusals in Scotland are naes

indicators.note: to start with means take the opening letters of the words

explanation.surface: A Scottish beauty spurns advances, with a teasing hint of heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses MY NAES into SEANYM; 'to start with' takes P and H. Aberdeen stands for Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea nymphs, such as the Nereids, are lovely female sea spirits of Greek myth.

clue.text: Crude fellows turning on mother with reproach

indicators.note: turning means facing the other way, so the word is reversed

parts.note: gits are coarse, contemptible men
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Coarse men rounding on their mother with blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses GITS to STIG. Git is British slang for an unpleasant man.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, a stain of shame or censure.
